problem: M vehicles do not traverse the claimed upstream feeder/observation domain
proposed_change: Within the existing geometry register an M insertion rule and observation domain that make qualified M vehicles traverse the required feeder; exact values pending B
fixed_factors: merge priority; lane-change and car-following parameters; TLS; ramp/urban storage; registered demands except necessary matched reference/challenge choice
predicted_observation: Qualified M vehicles traverse the registered common domain with complete entry/accounting; prospective M criteria can then be evaluated
refuting_or_inconclusive_observation: Registered travel domain is not achieved; or it is achieved but Q2/Q4 remain not_resolved
confounding_and_limit: Insertion changes travel time, merge arrival order, lane use and realized input; not a pure distance effect

problem: EJMI may be too narrow for intended-use impairment
proposed_change: Define a prospective M estimand with primary and supporting measures; do not relabel historical EJMI
predicted_observation: A qualified prospective comparison identifies consistent M impairment outside the old sufficient signature
refuting_or_inconclusive_observation: Prospective measures do not identify impairment or disagree across required seeds
confounding_and_limit: Old data are seen and can formulate but not independently confirm a new rule
next_gate: Retain as measurement component of H2 validation

problem: Post period contains delayed R/U entry
proposed_change: Register symmetric loading, observation and post windows based on actual entry/travel endpoints
fixed_factors: demand generation semantics and candidate topology except H2 necessary change
predicted_observation: Registered windows distinguish loading, delayed entry and recovery without calling an active-input period recovery
refuting_or_inconclusive_observation: R/U continue entering in the claimed recovery window or truncation remains material
confounding_and_limit: Changing insertion can change travel time and delayed-entry pattern

problem: Static merge priority and connection states may restrict R admission
proposed_change: Only if H2 validation cannot distinguish the obstacle, propose one isolated priority/connection contrast
fixed_factors: insertion domain, demand, TLS, storage, behavior parameters
predicted_observation: R admission changes in the registered direction while realized input and M domain remain qualified
refuting_or_inconclusive_observation: No qualified change or multiple coupled geometry/behavior changes prevent attribution
confounding_and_limit: No lane-change/gap-acceptance logs; static asymmetry is not causal proof
next_gate: Robert/new scoped proposal if H2 exhausts

problem: Downstream boundary could affect non-stopped performance
proposed_change: First inspect registered dynamic spatial evidence; redesign downstream only with observed boundary signature
fixed_factors: insertion, merge connection, TLS, storage and demand
predicted_observation: A registered downstream signature originates near the boundary and propagates upstream
refuting_or_inconclusive_observation: No registered boundary signature; present zero technical M stops already weaken the narrow queue claim
confounding_and_limit: Zero stops do not exclude non-stopped supply effects

problem: TLS context confounds shared R/U exposure
proposed_change: Retain movement-specific TLS and U outcomes; do not retime signal in current candidate
fixed_factors: TLS program, storage, demand and H2-unrelated factors
predicted_observation: U changes remain interpretable after stratifying the registered TLS context
refuting_or_inconclusive_observation: Observed changes are explained by signal context or temporal ordering is unavailable
confounding_and_limit: Co-occurrence cannot identify pure ramp-caused U loss
